title: AI and the Everything in the Whole Wide World Benchmark
benchmark_measurement: The paper does not measure any specific aspect of faith/religion. It is a position paper that critiques the concept of 'general' benchmarks in AI, arguing they have construct validity issues and cannot capture broad, general capabilities.
findings: The paper does not contain any explicit findings related to religion. Its central argument is that popular AI benchmarks, while presented as measures of general progress, are inherently specific, finite, and contextual, and suffer from issues like limited task design, subjectivity, and de-contextualization. These arguments could be applied to religious contexts, but the paper does not do so itself.
